takeaway: A pituitary adenoma compresses the optic chiasma, affecting the nasal retinal fibres and causing bitemporal hemianopia.

lines.text: A forty-eight-year-old man has persistent headaches early in the morning.
Recently he keeps bumping into the sides of doorways, and into people.
The tumour compresses the optic chiasma, and affects the nasal retinal fibres.
This causes bitemporal hemianopia: he loses the outer half of his vision on both sides.
That is why he bumps into things beside him.
So a pituitary adenoma presses on the optic chiasma.
